obligations.description: The fictional literal sample limit must match.

anchor.quote: The sample limit is declared below.

stages.label: authenticated-candidates
stages.explanation: Seven author jobs and six exact compositions carry local authorship; none has been accepted.

stages.label: generic-opinions-before-content
stages.explanation: The former editorial API can record opinions without inspecting the declared cross-file content.

stages.label: content-activation
stages.explanation: Content policy generation 1 advances governance to 3; generic old opinions no longer meet the current gate.

stages.label: formal-review-is-separate
stages.explanation: All seven inspected candidates pass formal runtime review; this does not establish declared content consistency.

stages.label: exact-pin-and-contributor-gate
stages.explanation: Every new decision must identify its exact content packet; a new reviewer grant does not separate its author principal.

stages.label: mismatch-blocked
stages.explanation: Document limit 4 and code limit 5 disagree despite the old generic approvals.

stages.label: unresolved-blocked
stages.explanation: A computed Python expression remains unresolved; the workflow never executes it.

stages.label: missing-quote-blocked
stages.explanation: A matching numeric relation does not repair the absent exact promise quotation.

stages.label: ambiguous-quote-blocked
stages.explanation: Two occurrences of the exact promise quotation make its anchor ambiguous.

stages.label: whole-bundle-required
stages.explanation: The bounded policy requires exactly its two configured write IDs; partial and extra bundles are blocked.

stages.label: eligible-before-policy-refresh
stages.explanation: Two noncontributor reviewers pin the exact packet for each write; decisions themselves do not alter that packet.

stages.label: policy-refresh-invalidates-opinions
stages.explanation: An identical policy body creates content generation 2 and governance generation 4; earlier pins cannot vote for the new packet.

stages.label: historical-decision-replay
stages.explanation: A current original grant can replay the exact historical operation; its old pin remains historical and a new operation rejects it.

stages.label: fresh-consideration-under-current-policy
stages.explanation: Both registered reviewers reconsider each write and pin the new packet; formal review, provenance and runtime guards remain separate requirements.

stages.label: accepted-with-content-receipt
stages.explanation: New acceptance checks the exact packet in its transaction, advances revision 1 to 2, and retains the packet referenced by receipt schema 3.

stages.label: historical-acceptance-is-stable
stages.explanation: The accepted candidate now has stale source reads; authorized replay returns its stored receipt before new live packet checks and creates no new event.

limitations: The SQLite owner, declared policy and local clock are trusted; local digests are not external attestation.
Programmed local principals and bearer grants do not establish people, models, expertise or independence.
Exact quotations and explicitly selected JSON/AST values do not prove natural-language entailment or factual truth.
The gate checks one declared whole bundle; it does not discover every undocumented requirement or artifact.
A literal relation match does not prove application behavior; computed code remains unresolved and is never executed.
Programmed consideration records explicit exact-packet approval but does not establish human understanding.
Public status is advisory; only the Store.accept transaction grants new runtime acceptance.
Historical replays preserve old packets and receipts without reviving old votes for a current policy.
Configured workers and seven jobs are not measured throughput or a supported limit of external agents.
Credentials, their hashes and SQLite stay private; this command creates no release or Git publication.
